question: Should OpenClaw make plugin-authored AI-safety events, the `safetyEventTypes` manifest capability, durable shared-state retention, and operator-query surfaces a permanent core contract now?
rationale: This is a new compatibility- and security-sensitive product boundary, not a mechanical correctness choice; the contributor has explicitly requested owner direction and the current repository policy requires owner judgment for broad plugin and persisted-state behavior.

options.title: Approve the complete core contract
options.body: Accept the plugin SDK, manifest permission, durable retention, Gateway/CLI/UI surfaces, and their long-term compatibility obligations as one supported feature.

options.title: Land a narrow core diagnostics seam first
options.body: Keep only the owner-approved internal/core diagnostic events now and defer the public plugin emitter, manifest permission, retention policy, and broad operator surfaces to a separately reviewed design.

options.title: Route the broader capability outside core
options.body: Keep core diagnostics generic and require the additional governance, UI, and plugin-specific observability workflow to be delivered through a plugin or external package.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow core diagnostics seam first
recommendation.body: Keep only the owner-approved internal/core diagnostic events now and defer the public plugin emitter, manifest permission, retention policy, and broad operator surfaces to a separately reviewed design.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly asks this person to decide the permanent plugin SDK and core-product boundary.
